scope_notes: Profile ml-system, not the suggested agent-tool: the repo is a fine-tuning, serving and benchmarking recipe for a 4B 'System One' classifier whose product (Prompt48/my-jev-4b) is published on Hugging Face (README.md:3-13). SEC-5 is NA because no CI exists.

gaps.title: Documented smoke test publishes to Hugging Face
gaps.case: README.md:54 runs 'bash train.sh --max_train 200'; train.sh:7 always passes --hf_repo "$HF_REPO"; train_unsloth.py:220-236 then pushes merged weights, the LoRA adapter and a new README to HF_REPO. recording/03_smoke.sh:3 avoids it with --hf_repo '', the README does not.
gaps.impact: Following the quickstart overwrites the published model and its model card with a 200-row smoke-test model.
gaps.fix: Make publishing opt-in (a --push flag) or skip it when --max_train is set; show --hf_repo '' in the README smoke test.

gaps.title: Public endpoint falls back to a well-known API key
gaps.case: serve.sh:10 binds 0.0.0.0:8000 and serve.sh:17 uses --api-key "${MY_JEV_API_KEY:-local}"; .env.example:7 ships the key empty; README.md:37-38,75 tells users to expose port 8000 through the RunPod proxy.
gaps.impact: Unauthorised use of the GPU endpoint (cost, availability) whenever the key is left unset.
gaps.fix: Fail closed: refuse to start when the key is empty or 'local', or generate a random key during setup.

gaps.title: Base-model results have no committed measurement
gaps.case: README.md:18-27 reports base Qwen3.5-4B figures (63.9%, 60.0%, 70.0%, 70.4%, 63.0%, ECE 0.144, 113 ms); results/ holds only bench_pod, bench_laptop and train_report.json, and .gitignore:7 ignores bench_base/. No results file carries a date, commit or model revision.
gaps.impact: 7 of the 24 headline cells cannot be checked from the repository; results cannot be tied to a model revision.
gaps.fix: Commit bench_base/report.json and the per-row JSONL; add date, repo commit, model revision and vLLM version to every report.

gaps.title: Probability extraction can overwrite label probabilities
gaps.case: bench.py:85-87 builds {token.strip(): p} from top_logprobs: tokens equal after strip() overwrite rather than add (the later, lower-ranked one wins when the list is ordered by probability), and labels outside the top 20 count as 0 before renormalisation. Jev's probabilities come from its API (bench.py:106-108). The same fine-tuned model scores ECE 0.048 with in-process softmax over option letters (results/train_report.json:46) and 0.212 in the bench (results/bench_pod/report.json:14), on different task mixes.
gaps.impact: The calibration row (README.md:25) may reflect the extraction method rather than the model, and compares two different probability methods.
gaps.fix: Sum probabilities per stripped label or request the exact label tokens; report tev1_dev-only ECE from both harnesses; state the method next to the number.

gaps.title: Invalid answers are scored as the first option
gaps.case: bench.py:89-93: when no option label appears in top_logprobs and the text matches no label, every probability is 0; bench.py:136 max(probs, key=probs.get) then returns the first option key, and the row is ok=True, so the report shows errors 0.
gaps.impact: Off-list outputs silently become predictions, biasing accuracy and hiding how often the model leaves the answer format.
gaps.fix: Mark such rows invalid, count them in the report, and exclude them from calibration or score them explicitly as wrong.

gaps.title: No checkpoints in a 282-minute training run
gaps.case: train_unsloth.py:194 sets save_strategy='no'; HF_TOKEN is read only after training (train_unsloth.py:221); bench rows are written after all tasks finish (bench.py:152-154). results/train_report.json:4 records 282.2 minutes.
gaps.impact: A pod interruption loses the whole run (about $2.30 at $0.49/h) and any partial benchmark; a missing token is discovered only after training.
gaps.fix: Use save_strategy='steps' with resume_from_checkpoint, validate HF_TOKEN at start, append bench rows as they complete.

gaps.title: Unpinned dependencies, dataset and installer
gaps.case: setup_pod.sh:8 pipes the uv installer to sh; setup_pod.sh:14,19 install unsloth, vllm and others without versions; setup_pod.sh:23 clones tev1 at HEAD; train_unsloth.py:38 loads the base model without a revision.
gaps.impact: Results cannot be reproduced at the reviewed commit; upstream changes alter data, training and serving silently.
gaps.fix: Lock dependencies with hashes, pin the tev1 commit and base-model revision, verify the installer checksum.

gaps.title: Published model card asserts a license and omits known weaknesses
gaps.case: model_card.py:9 declares license apache-2.0 while model_card.py:77-81 says the data sources' licenses must be checked before commercial use; the card reports only held-out dev results (model_card.py:24-33), not the phishing drop of README.md:21,30, and does not link the training repo (model_card.py:75).
gaps.impact: Users of the published model receive a permissive license claim and in-distribution-only results; model documentation expected for published models is incomplete.
gaps.fix: Derive the model license from the data licenses, add limitations and out-of-distribution results, link repo and commit.

gaps.title: Decision contract duplicated and unversioned
gaps.case: The exact system prompt and JSON message format are copied in bench.py:33-35, train_unsloth.py:29-31 and model_card.py:45-47; there is no schema for task or response; model_card.py:68-69 warns that any deviation changes behaviour.
gaps.impact: A client or agent that drifts from the prose contract gets different behaviour without an error.
gaps.fix: One shared contract file (prompt version plus JSON schema for task and response) imported by all three and published with the model.

opportunities.title: One calibration-metric module instead of two
opportunities.description: ECE and Brier are implemented twice (bench.py:163-174 and train_unsloth.py:112-120) on different probability sources, giving 0.048 and 0.212 for the same model on different mixes. laya (a System 1 decision engine trained against proper scoring rules, per its README) and RE4exa's rex calibrate compute the same metrics. One tested module with intervals removes the discrepancy and serves all three.

opportunities.title: Shared System-1 decision benchmark with laya and laya-coreml
opportunities.description: my-jev's suites (tev1 dev stratified by source plus three third-party sets, bench.py:51-69) and task shape (state, question, options with label, key, description) match the typed single-pass decisions laya describes. Publishing the suite with pinned data and the JSONL row format as a common answer key would let both models, and on-device laya-coreml, be compared on identical tasks including abstention.

opportunities.title: On-device decision gate
opportunities.description: The --gguf path (train_unsloth.py:51,226-229) and one-token output make a local 4B classifier for routine agent decisions that never sends state to a cloud API. Quantised accuracy and calibration are unmeasured; running q4_k_m and q8_0 through the 747-task suite would show whether the local path holds.

opportunities.title: Advisory tool-risk screen inside agent-sandbox-lockdown approvals
opportunities.description: agent-sandbox-lockdown (same author) gates writes behind human approval and logs every tool call (its README). my-jev scores 88.3% on the third-party tool-risk suite (results/bench_pod/report.json:9); used only to annotate or order approval prompts, never to auto-approve, it adds a cheap local signal without weakening the human gate. It needs an abstention threshold first.

questions.question: Does the README results table match the committed benchmark reports?
questions.answer: Yes for the my-jev-4b and TypeSafe Jev columns (results/bench_pod and results/bench_laptop); the base-model column has no committed report and no result is dated.

questions.question: Did fine-tuning improve the model, and where did it regress?
questions.answer: In distribution it improved (tev1 dev 85.8% vs 63.9% base); overall it trails TypeSafe Jev (70.8% vs 75.5%), and it is worse than the base model on phishing (47.7% vs 60.0%) and calibration (ECE 0.212 vs 0.144). The README states the first two; the calibration regression is shown but not discussed.

questions.question: Can the recipe be followed safely and reproduced as documented?
questions.answer: Not without care: the README smoke test publishes to Hugging Face, the server falls back to a default API key on a public port, training keeps no checkpoints, and dependencies, dataset and base model are unpinned.

not_examined: Published Hugging Face artefacts (Prompt48/my-jev-4b, -lora): no web access
tev1 upstream dataset scripts and their source licenses
Telemetry defaults of vLLM and huggingface_hub
Runtime behaviour: nothing was run (static review), so the logprob-overwrite effect is unquantified
Git history beyond the single shallow commit
